title: Sick Simon by Dan Krall (Personal Health & Hygiene) #toddlers #kindergarten #education #kidsbooks
fulltitle: Sick Simon by Dan Krall (Personal Health & Hygiene) #toddlers #kindergarten #education #kidsbooks
description:
"Sick Simon" is a clever, humorous, and slightly gross picture book written and illustrated by Dan Krall. It tells the story of a young boy named Simon who is excited to be sick.

Unlike most kids, Simon loves everything about being ill—the days off school, the cozy blankets, and the special treatment. He's so enthusiastic that he actively tries to stay sick by embracing his germs. He coughs without covering his mouth, doesn't wash his hands, and even kisses his family members goodnight, proudly spreading his germs everywhere.

The story takes a fantastical turn when Simon's germs—personified as cute, googly-eyed monsters—start talking to him. They reveal that they are using him as a paradise and a vehicle to spread to his friends, family, and entire town. At first, Simon is proud of his "accomplishment," but he soon realizes the consequences: his whole class, his teacher, and even his family get sick, ruining a much-anticipated field trip.

In the end, Simon decides to fight back against his germs by adopting healthy habits, ultimately learning how to be sick responsibly.

Themes and Lessons
"Sick Simon" is a powerful tool for teaching children about health and empathy in a way that is engaging and memorable, not preachy.

1. Personal Health and Hygiene
This is the most direct theme. The book serves as a fun, illustrated guide to basic hygiene practices. It explicitly shows why actions like covering your coughs, washing your hands, and using tissues are important.

Lesson: Good hygiene isn't just a rule; it's a way to keep yourself and others healthy.

2. Empathy and Community Responsibility
The book brilliantly shifts the focus from the individual ("I get to stay home!") to the community ("Oh no, I got everyone else sick!"). Simon's journey is about understanding that his actions have consequences for those around him.

Lesson: We have a responsibility to our friends, family, and community to try not to spread germs. It's about caring for others.

3. Cause and Effect
Krall masterfully illustrates the chain reaction of sickness. Simon's one set of germs leads to his whole class getting ill, which then cancels a fun event for everyone.

Lesson: Your choices can create a ripple effect, impacting more people than you might realize.

4. Knowledge is Power
The book demystifies germs by giving them a personality. Instead of being an abstract, scary concept, germs are shown as tangible creatures that can be understood and managed. By knowing how germs spread, Simon gains the power to fight them.

Lesson: Understanding how you get sick and how sickness spreads is the first step to preventing it.

How the Book Achieves Its Goal
Humor and the "Gross-Out" Factor: The illustrations of the colorful, slimy germs and Simon's unabashedly snotty behavior are hilarious to children. This "gross" factor grabs their attention and makes the lesson stick far better than a simple lecture.

Personification of Germs: By making the germs cute and giving them voices, the abstract concept of illness becomes concrete and understandable for a young child. It turns a health lesson into a story about a battle between a boy and his microscopic monsters.

Relatable Protagonist: Every child has been sick and can relate to the mixed feelings of misery and the small comforts that come with it. Simon is not a villain; he's just a kid who doesn't understand the bigger picture, making his eventual realization more impactful.

In Summary
"Sick Simon" is more than just a book about washing your hands. It's a story about growing from selfishness to selflessness. It teaches children that being part of a community means looking out for each other, and that sometimes, the simplest acts of hygiene are profound acts of kindness. It's a modern classic for parents and teachers looking for a fun, effective way to discuss health and empathy.

description:
Here is a detailed overview of Dan Santat's award-winning picture book, After the Fall.
After the Fall (How Humpty Dumpty Got Back Up Again) is a creative and heartfelt sequel to the classic nursery rhyme "Humpty Dumpty." The book begins where the original rhyme ends: after Humpty Dumpty's great fall from the wall.

The story follows Humpty as an anxious and cautious bird-watcher who loves being close to the birds but is now terrified of heights. He leads a safe, but limited, life on the ground, missing his favorite pastime of watching the birds from the high wall. The book chronicles his journey of overcoming fear, trauma, and anxiety to reclaim his life. It’s a story about resilience, courage, and the transformative power of getting back up after a setback.

Theme
The central theme of After the Fall is resilience and overcoming adversity. Santat explores this through several interconnected ideas:

Living with Fear and Anxiety: The book is a powerful metaphor for dealing with the aftermath of a traumatic event. Humpty isn't just physically scarred; he's psychologically scarred. His world has become small and governed by fear.

The Limitations of "Safety": Humpty creates a safe, controlled life for himself, but this safety comes at a cost. He is no longer doing the things he loves. The book suggests that while being cautious is understandable, a life ruled solely by fear is not a full life.

Persistence and Courage: The title itself, "How Humpty Dumpty Got Back Up Again," signals that this is a story about process. It's not about being fearless; it's about being brave enough to try again despite the fear.

Transformation and Self-Discovery: Humpty's journey isn't just about getting back to where he was. His fall and his struggle to overcome it fundamentally change him, leading to a surprising and empowering transformation.

Lesson
The primary lesson of After the Fall is that our struggles and failures do not define us; what defines us is how we choose to move forward from them.

More specifically, the book teaches:

It's okay to be scared. Acknowledging fear is the first step.

Healing is a process. Humpty doesn't just climb the wall again overnight. He takes small, incremental steps (like making a paper airplane), and he has setbacks (when the airplane gets stuck).

Courage is action in the face of fear. True bravery isn't the absence of fear, but the decision that something else (like passion, joy, or fulfillment) is more important.

Sometimes, when we "put ourselves back together," we become something new and stronger. The book's stunning climax reveals that Humpty doesn't just become the egg he was before. He hatches into a bird, capable of flight. This symbolizes that by facing our fears, we can discover strengths we never knew we had.

The Powerful Ending
The ending is crucial to understanding the book's message. Humpty, determined to retrieve his paper airplane, painstakingly builds a new, sturdier wall out of cardboard boxes. When he reaches the top, he doesn't just get his airplane back. He takes a leap of faith and hatches into a bird, finally achieving the flight he had always admired from afar.

This twist redefines the meaning of his original fall. It wasn't just a tragic accident; it was a necessary crack that allowed for his eventual transformation and freedom. It’s a profound message for readers of all ages: our cracks and breaks don't have to be permanent scars; they can be the very things that allow us to become who we are meant to be.

In summary, After the Fall is much more than a nursery rhyme continuation. It is a deeply empathetic and inspiring guide to navigating fear and failure, making it a timeless story for both children and adults.
